clue.text: Engineer claims idea involving old interactive websites

to engineer is to contrive or rework, so the letters of these two words are rearranged

explanation.surface: Someone is told to rework a plan that takes in something outdated.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Engineer' looks like a noun giving orders, but it is the signal to rearrange the two words that follow.
explanation.definitionFit: Platforms like Facebook and Twitter are online sites where users interact and share content, the core sense of the phrase.

clue.text: Support American being consumed by shame

indicators.note: being consumed by means swallowed up, so one piece sits inside another

parts.note: a stain is a mark of shame or disgrace

explanation.surface: An American's backing evaporates because of a disgrace.
explanation.definitionFit: To sustain something is to bear its weight or keep it going, a synonym of support.

clue.text: School bus many regularly filled, forming queue

indicators.note: regularly means at even intervals, so every other letter of these words is taken

explanation.surface: A crowded school bus with children lining up to board.
explanation.walkthrough: 'regularly' takes the even letters of SCHOOL BUS MANY; 'filled' and 'forming' are padding that links to the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: A column is a line of people or vehicles one behind another, just as a queue is.

clue.text: Relative having a cheerful manner without any frills

indicators.note: frills are edging trims, so the word loses its outer letters

parts.note: jaunty means sprightly and cheerful in manner

explanation.surface: A plain, cheerful family member who dislikes fuss.
explanation.walkthrough: 'without any frills' strips the first and last letters from JAUNTY.
explanation.definitionFit: An aunt is a parent's sister, one example of a family relative.

clue.text: Anger breaks over TV chef in Maine making US trailer

indicators.note: in places the whole construction inside the state abbreviation

parts.note: ME is the postal abbreviation for the US state of Maine

indicators.note: breaks means bursts into, so this piece is inserted into the next

parts.note: O is the cricket scoring abbreviation for an over
Ken Hom is a television chef known for Chinese cooking
bile is bitterness or bad temper

explanation.surface: A furious outburst interrupts a celebrity cook's visit to New England.
explanation.walkthrough: Two insertions nest: 'breaks' works first, then 'in' wraps the result. Ken Hom is a long-running BBC cookery presenter.
explanation.definitionFit: In American usage a mobile home is a large trailer used as a permanent dwelling.

clue.text: Party with peanuts provided regularly for Will, maybe?

parts.note: a do is an informal party
cum is Latin for with, as in 'bedroom-cum-study'

indicators.note: regularly means at even intervals, so alternate letters of the word are kept

explanation.surface: A party where peanuts are put out at intervals for a guest named Will.
explanation.walkthrough: 'regularly' takes the even letters of PEANUTS; 'provided' is padding. 'Will' looks like a man's name.
explanation.definitionFit: A will is a legal paper setting out how an estate is shared, one example of an official document.

clue.text: No fewer than fifty invading a revolutionary state

indicators.note: invading means entering, so this piece goes inside the other
revolutionary means overturning, so the word's letters are rearranged

parts.note: L is the Roman numeral for fifty

explanation.surface: Fifty fighters invade a country in revolt.
explanation.walkthrough: 'revolutionary' turns STATE into TEAST; 'invading' puts L inside A TEAST.
explanation.definitionFit: The phrase sets a minimum, so it means the amount is that many or more.

clue.text: Greek character from university returning cured of speech impediment?

indicators.note: returning means going back, so the letters are read in reverse

parts.note: someone cured of a speech impediment has no lisp

explanation.surface: A student back from university whose stammer has been cured.
explanation.walkthrough: 'returning' reverses NO LISP to give PSILON after U.
explanation.definitionFit: Upsilon is the twentieth letter of the Greek alphabet.

clue.text: Absolute timing a duet represented

indicators.note: represented means presented again in another form, so the letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: Two singers perform a duet with perfect timing.
explanation.walkthrough: 'represented' rearranges TIMING A DUET.
explanation.definitionFit: Unmitigated means not softened at all, so total or out-and-out, as absolute does.

clue.text: Rural virus, mostly accompanied by stomach pain

indicators.note: mostly means all but the last bit, so the final letter goes

parts.note: a bug is an informal term for a virus
colic is acute pain in the abdomen

explanation.surface: A country illness: a virus that brings stomach cramps.
explanation.walkthrough: 'mostly' cuts BUG to BU.
explanation.definitionFit: Bucolic describes the countryside and pastoral life, the same sense as rural.

clue.text: Honour Holland typically announced displaying royal finery

parts.note: to crown someone is to honour them

indicators.note: announced means spoken out, so the name is heard rather than seen

parts.note: Jools Holland is a well-known British pianist and TV presenter, a typical bearer of the name

explanation.walkthrough: 'announced' turns JOOLS into JEWELS. Jools Holland hosts the BBC music show 'Later'; 'typically' marks him as one example of a JOOLS.
explanation.definitionFit: The crown jewels are the regalia of the monarch, the grandest of royal adornments.

clue.text: Unpleasant atmosphere when old lady goes behind this writer's back

indicators.note: goes behind means comes after, so the following pieces sit after the first
back means turned round, so these letters are read in reverse

parts.note: this writer is the setter, I; this writer's is I'M
as can mean when, as in 'as I left'
ma is an informal word for mother, an old lady

explanation.surface: A grumble about an unpleasant mood when the writer's mother talks behind their back.
explanation.walkthrough: 'back' looks like the body part being talked behind, but it turns the setter's 'I'm' round.
explanation.definitionFit: A miasma is a noxious vapour, or figuratively an oppressive atmosphere.

clue.text: Backache after beginning to prune plant

indicators.note: after means coming later, so the second piece follows the first
beginning to means the opening letter of the next word is taken

parts.note: lumbago is pain in the lower back

explanation.surface: A gardener's backache after pruning.
explanation.walkthrough: 'after' puts LUMBAGO behind P from 'beginning to prune'. 'Plant' looks like a verb but names the answer.
explanation.definitionFit: Plumbago is a flowering shrub, also called leadwort, so it is a kind of garden plant.

clue.text: Uncle, man lacking money and close to despair

parts.note: a man is a chess piece, such as a pawn
broke means having no money

indicators.note: close to means the end of the next word, so its final letter is taken

explanation.surface: A relative who is skint and nearly in despair.
explanation.walkthrough: 'close to' takes R from DESPAIR. 'Uncle' is old slang for a pawnbroker.
explanation.definitionFit: Uncle is old British slang for the person who lends money against pledged goods.

clue.text: Mix 3 ingredients for sandwich filling

indicators.note: to mix is to stir together, so the letters are rearranged

parts.note: the ingredients of 3 are the letters of the answer to 3-down, a relative

explanation.surface: A recipe: blend three items to fill a sandwich.
explanation.walkthrough: '3' is a cross-reference to 3-down, not a number; 'Mix' rearranges its letters.
explanation.definitionFit: Tinned fish, often with mayonnaise, is a classic sandwich filler.

clue.text: President observed going around hotel in grand fashion

indicators.note: going around means turning back, so these letters are read in reverse

parts.note: to have observed something is to have saw it, past tense see
H is hotel in the NATO phonetic alphabet
G is short for grand, a thousand
ton is an old word for high fashion

explanation.surface: A president is spotted touring a hotel in fine style.
explanation.walkthrough: 'going around' looks like touring the hotel, but it turns the first word round. 'Ton', from French, is an old term for high fashion.
explanation.definitionFit: George Washington was the first President of the United States.

clue.text: Briefly test coupling that holds new rotating pin

indicators.note: briefly means cut short, so the last letter is dropped

parts.note: to try something is to test it

indicators.note: that holds means containing, so the next piece goes inside

parts.note: a union is a joining or coupling

explanation.surface: An engineer quickly tests a joint fitted with a new swivelling pin.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Briefly' drops the last letter of the synonym for test; 'that holds' signals the container.
explanation.definitionFit: A trunnion is a pivot projecting from each side of a cannon or cylinder, letting it swivel.

clue.text: Many got so confused about right art of fine dining

confused means mixed up, so the letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: Many diners get muddled about what correct fine dining involves.
explanation.walkthrough: 'confused' rearranges MANY GOT SO; 'about' puts it round R.
explanation.definitionFit: Gastronomy is the practice or art of choosing, cooking and eating good food.

clue.text: Go to work, perhaps?

explanation.walkthrough: 'Go to work' reads as a commute, but it describes how 'go' stands to 'work': each means 'function'.
explanation.definitionFit: A word with the same meaning as another, as go is for work, is the relation named.

clue.text: Wife quits golf club in bitterness

parts.note: a wedge is a lofted golf club

explanation.surface: A wife bitterly leaves the golf club.
explanation.walkthrough: 'quits' removes W from WEDGE; 'golf club' looks like the venue.
explanation.definitionFit: Edge in a voice or remark is a sharp, cutting quality, akin to bitterness.

clue.text: Clerics decide a Conservative is accommodating

explanation.surface: Church officials vote a Tory in.
explanation.walkthrough: 'is accommodating' signals the answer inside 'deciDE A CONServative'.
explanation.definitionFit: Deacons are ordained ministers ranking below priests, so they are clergy.

clue.text: Band of very cold weather reported

indicators.note: reported means spoken, so the word is heard rather than seen

parts.note: a freeze is a spell of very cold weather

explanation.surface: A band of icy weather is forecast.
explanation.walkthrough: 'reported' turns FREEZE into its sound-alike.
explanation.definitionFit: A frieze is a decorated horizontal strip along a wall, a band of ornament.

clue.text: Number really discontented over worker's status as rent payer

explanation.walkthrough: 'discontented' empties REALLY to RY.
explanation.definitionFit: Tenantry is the condition of holding property as a tenant, someone who pays rent.

clue.text: Dubbing for film musical

definitions.meaning: dubbing, a variant of dubbin, is a greasy preparation for softening leather
The 1978 film musical with John Travolta

explanation.walkthrough: 'Dubbing' suggests adding a soundtrack; it is the leather dressing.
explanation.definitionFit: Dubbin is a fat that waterproofs leather, and the musical is a famous title.

clue.text: Star doesn't go conversing in Spanish

explanation.walkthrough: The second reading splits the answer as NO VA, Spanish for 'it doesn't go', echoing the Vauxhall Nova car myth.
explanation.definitionFit: A nova is a star whose brightness rises suddenly; the Spanish phrase gives the same letters.

clue.text: Pester captain boldly going to effect military evacuation

Captain Kirk of Star Trek boldly goes where no man has gone before

explanation.walkthrough: 'boldly going' recalls the Star Trek opening line.
explanation.definitionFit: Dunkirk was the 1940 evacuation of Allied troops from France, a famous military withdrawal.

clue.text: Demanding individual, ultimately manager to you and me

parts.note: one means a single individual

parts.note: us is you and me together

explanation.walkthrough: 'ultimately' takes the last letters of MANAGER and TO, giving RO.
explanation.definitionFit: Onerous means burdensome, needing great effort, as a demanding task does.

clue.text: They discern thoughts of fear stopping workers going underground

indicators.note: stopping means plugging a gap, so this piece goes inside the other

parts.note: miners work underground
dread is great fear
